parameters.content:
## Before the first run

**1. Credentials**
* Every `Pn · Fetch Tickets` and `Pn · Fetch Metrics + Users` -> select that brand's **Zendesk** credential. There are two per brand.
* The three `Gemini ...` nodes -> select the **Google Gemini (PaLM) API** credential. If the list is empty, switch *Authentication* to **Generic -> Header Auth** and use header `x-goog-api-key`.
* `Slack · Personality` -> select the Slack credential and the target channel.

**2. Workflow settings**
* Timezone must be **UTC**.
* Set your existing **Error Workflow** so failures raise the usual Slack alert.

**3. Zendesk tag (required for the Assisted metric)**
Add a tag - default name `automation_replied` - to the ticket whenever John posts a **public** comment, from inside your existing CS automation.
Until that tag exists, `Assisted` reads 0 and those tickets are counted as `Fully manual`. The report prints a warning line while the tag is unconfigured.

**4. Backfill / testing**
`Compute Window` -> raise `LOOKBACK_DAYS` and execute manually. Set it back to 1 afterwards.

**5. Tuning the examples**
`max_quotes` (10), `quote_chars` (300), `tech_quotes_per_cluster` (10) and `tech_quotes_max` (30) live in each project's Config node. If a report would exceed Slack's 40k limit the formatter automatically rebuilds it with shorter quotes and says so; if that is still not enough, lower `max_quotes` or `tech_quotes_max`.

## Adding a project

1. Select the six `Pn · ...` nodes of any existing brand -> copy -> paste. Rename the prefix to the next free `Pn`.
2. In `P2 · Config` set `project_key`, `project_display_name`, `zendesk_base`, `category_field_id`, `automation_agent_id`.
   * No automation on that project -> set `automation_agent_id` to **0**. The report drops the automation block and collapses performance to one column.
   * Odd category slugs -> put them in `category_override_map` as JSON, e.g. `{"weird_slug":"refunds"}`. Leave `""` when there are none.
3. Point `P2 · Fetch Tickets` / `P2 · Fetch Metrics + Users` at that project's Zendesk credential.
4. Fix the two internal references inside the pasted Code nodes so they name the **P2** nodes, not P1.
5. Connect `Compute Window` -> `P2 · Config`, and `P2 · Assemble` -> `All Projects`.
6. On the `All Projects` Merge node, raise **Number of Inputs** by one and connect the new `Assemble` to it.
7. Add a rule to `Route by Project` and a Slack node for the new channel.

Pausing a project: disable its `Config` node. The whole branch is skipped.

## How the numbers are produced

**Cohort** - every ticket whose `created_at` falls in the previous UTC day. Every figure describes that cohort, so `Solved` is really *same-day* solved: a ticket received yesterday and solved tomorrow is never counted. Consistent, but always lower than the lifetime resolution rate.

**Solved** = status `solved` or `closed`. **Performance** is computed over solved tickets only, split three ways: `Auto` (John solved), `Assisted` (John commented, human solved), `Manual` (John never touched it).

**Times** are Zendesk calendar minutes, never business hours. Averages are shown next to medians because one stalled ticket wrecks a mean.

**Agent replies** = `metric_sets.replies`, i.e. public agent replies. One-touch = exactly one reply.

**Reopen rate** has its own denominator. A ticket solved and then reopened is currently `open`, so it is not in `Solved` - the rate is measured against everything that reached solved at least once. The `Reopened` line in VOLUME splits by who solved it, which is the fastest way to see whether the automation is closing tickets prematurely.

**Refund sub-lines** are generated per refund category, with labels derived from the slug rather than hardcoded, so a new refund option in Zendesk appears on its own line automatically.

**Category buckets** are mapped in every `Pn · Assemble` node (`CATEGORY_MAP`). Slugs are normalised first - lowercased, runs of non-alphanumerics collapsed to one `_` - so `cancellation___subscription` and `special_offers/discounts` both match. `spam` and `duplicate_contact` are counted but excluded from the percentage denominator. A new Zendesk option that nothing matches shows up as a loud `Unmapped categories` line instead of disappearing.

**Gemini never counts and never selects alone.** It does two jobs: it scores tickets 1-5 for how much actionable product feedback they contain, and it discovers technical issue labels (pass 1) then assigns tickets to them (pass 2). The final choice of which tickets to quote, and every tally, happens in code. Ids that do not appear in the input are discarded. Any technical ticket it fails to classify falls into `Other`, so totals always reconcile. The taxonomy is rediscovered daily, so labels are not comparable day to day - freeze the list in config once it stabilises if you want trends.

**Example tickets.** Each category shows up to `max_quotes` real tickets, each capped at `quote_chars` characters, with a link to the ticket and the requester's email. A category with fewer tickets than the limit skips the model call entirely and shows all of them.

**Technical examples** appear only in the TECHNICAL ISSUES section, grouped under their cluster, and are allocated differently: at or below `max_quotes` every technical ticket is quoted, and above it each cluster gets up to `tech_quotes_per_cluster` (default 10), allocated one round at a time so every cluster is guaranteed at least one example before `tech_quotes_max` (default 30) closes the section. A cluster holding a single ticket still shows it. That means no issue type is ever left without an example - including the `Other` fallback, which holds the tickets the taxonomy missed and is usually the most interesting one. Clustering itself always covers every technical ticket, so the counts are complete regardless of how many are quoted.

**Why the message is part monospace and part not:** Slack refuses to render links inside a code block, so the metrics tables are fenced (they need column alignment) and the breakdown is not (it needs clickable ticket links).

**Only ticket id, subject and the first 240 characters of the opening message** are sent to Gemini. Requester emails are attached in code afterwards, so they never reach the model. No names, no full threads.

**Quote hygiene:** quoted reply chains, signature blocks after a `--` line and reply headers are stripped before a ticket is quoted, then the body is collapsed to one line.

**Zero-ticket day** still sends a report, with zeros. A *failed* Zendesk call sends a short failure notice instead of fake zeros, and leaves the other projects alone.
